original.reason: The asserted odd-case construction is invalid: odd n does not make multiplication by an arbitrary d_i invertible modulo n; its claimed column terms are not constant across rows; and no relation among the independent row AP parameters is established. The even case also leaves its essential obstruction as an unproved “case-by-case” claim, with a stated intersection assertion that is false in general. Thus the conclusion is unsupported.

judgment.reason: The central interlacing lemma is essentially the theorem and is not proved. Cyclic shifts of ranks in arbitrary, unrelated row arithmetic progressions do not by themselves imply that column entries have a common difference. The even-case parity discussion also does not establish the claimed impossibility.

Its “interlacing lemma” is asserted with only a vague cyclic-shift description. No calculation shows that fixed-column entries from arbitrary AP parts have constant difference. The even parity argument does not yield the alleged contradiction: a single column can meet the first two parts once each while having odd common difference.

Calling the key assertion a standard lemma does not prove it. The proposed rank arrangement does not establish arithmetic-progression columns for arbitrary partitions, and the even-case counting claim is neither supplied nor justified. These are material gaps.

Both parts rest on an unproved finite interlacing lemma. The claimed orientation compatibility and constant column differences are asserted without derivation, while the even-case statement that alternation forces two terms into the initial blocks is unsupported and not a consequence of parity alone.
